passages.text: Trachycarpus martianus (also known as Martius' fan palm) is a tree in the family Arecaceae. There are two distinct populations: one at {{convert|1500|m|ft|-3|abbr=on}} in the Khasia Hills of Meghalaya state, in northeast India, the other at {{convert|2400|m|ft|-3|abbr=on}} in central northern Nepal. Other populations have been reported in Assam, Sikkim, Burma and southern China. The main identifying characteristics are the regular leaf splits (to about halfway), the coffee-bean-shaped seeds (similar looking to Trachycarpus latisectus) and the bare, as opposed to fibrous trunk. The new leaf spear and edges of the petioles are covered with a white tomentum.
The species is named after the German botanist Carl Friedrich Philipp von Martius (1794-1868).
It is used in making Jhapi, a traditional head cover often used to felicitate guests in Assam.
